Write /root/bench-runs/h6-cf69a106/test/jsonpatch.test.mjs: a node:test suite (Node 22, built-ins only: `node:test`, `node:assert/strict`; NO npm install) for the library /root/bench-runs/h6-cf69a106/jsonpatch.mjs (import { parsePointer, applyPatch, PatchError } from '../jsonpatch.mjs'). Read jsonpatch.mjs first. DO NOT edit jsonpatch.mjs or jsonpatch-cli.mjs. Ignore scratch/. Do not touch test/cli.test.mjs (another helper writes it). Load skill tdd-workflow if available.

Rules: tests must be strict — assert exact values with assert.deepStrictEqual / strictEqual (deepStrictEqual distinguishes -0 from 0 via Object.is; for -0 also check Object.is(x, -0) explicitly). Check member order with assert.deepStrictEqual(Object.keys(x), [...]). Use helpers `expectPatchError(fn, message, index)` that asserts thrown error `instanceof PatchError`, `instanceof Error`, `.name === 'PatchError'`, exact `.message`, and `.index` strictly equal (null or number). Keep functions small; split into describe() blocks; file may be up to ~600 lines. No console.log. If a test fails against the implementation, DO NOT weaken it — report it to me with the failing assertion.

Spec cases to cover (each must be a test a plausible wrong implementation would fail):

parsePointer
- "" → []; "/" → [""]; "/a//b/" → ["a","","b",""]; "/~01" → ["~1"]; "/~10" → ["/0"]; "/a~0b~1c" → ["a~b/c"]; "/~0~1" → ["~/"]. Returns a new array each call (two calls not ===, mutate one doesn't affect next).
- SyntaxError exactly message 'invalid pointer' (assert.throws with {name:'SyntaxError', message:'invalid pointer'} and instanceof SyntaxError): "a", " /a", "/~", "/~2", "/a~", "/~/", "#/a".
- TypeError 'pointer must be a string' for: undefined, null, 1, ['/a'], new String('/a'), {}, Symbol? (skip symbol), true.

applyPatch errors
- non-array patch: null, undefined, {}, '[]', new String(''), {length:0}, an array-like → PatchError 'patch must be an array', index null (strictEqual null).
- form reasons with index: 'operation 0: not an object' for null, [], 5, 'x', a function, undefined; a hole: `[ {op:'test',path:'',value:1}, , ]`? careful: build `const p = [valid]; p.length = 2;` → 'operation 1: not an object' index 1. String object `Object.assign(new String('x'), {op:'add', path:'/a', value:1})` on {} → succeeds giving {a:1}. Date with own op/path/value also accepted.
- bad op: missing op; op 'ADD'; op ' add'; op new String('add'); op inherited (Object.create({op:'add'}) plus own path/value); op 'get'. Non-enumerable own op is counted: Object.defineProperty({path:'/a', value:1}, 'op', {value:'add', enumerable:false}) applied to {} → {a:1}. Likewise non-enumerable own `value` and `path` count.
- bad path: missing; path 5; path new String('/a'); path 'a'; path '/~2'; inherited path.
- bad from: move and copy with from missing / not string / String object / invalid '/~' / inherited. `from` on add is ignored even if invalid ({op:'add',path:'/a',value:1,from:5} ok). `value` on remove ignored even if undefined-valued (own value undefined ok).
- missing value: add/replace/test without value; value: null is present (add null works → {a:null}); inherited value doesn't count → 'missing value'.
- cannot remove root: {op:'remove', path:''}.
- cannot move into own child: from '/a' path '/a/b'; from '' path '/a'; from '' path '/' ; NOT for from '/a' path '/ab' (that one just runs: on {a:1} → {ab:1}); NOT for from '/a' path '/a' (no-op); from '/a/b' path '/a' allowed.
- reason precedence: op missing and path missing → 'bad op'; move with bad path and bad from → 'bad path'; add with bad path and no value → 'bad path'; remove path '' on a String object fine; move from '' path '/x' AND also everything else fine → own child.
- All ops validated up front: patch [ {op:'add', path:'/a', value:1}, {op:'test', path:'/zzz', value:1}, {op:'bogus'} ] → 'operation 2: bad op' index 2 (not test failed at 1). And apply stops at first failure: [{op:'remove',path:'/x'},{op:'remove', path:'/~'}] → 'operation 1: bad path'.
- doc and patch not mutated, also when throwing: deep-freeze-free check: take structuredClone snapshots of doc and patch, run a patch whose op 0 add/remove/replace succeeds and op 1 fails (test failed), assert doc and patch deepStrictEqual their snapshots. Also with successful patch. Also Object.isFrozen approach: Object.freeze deeply the doc and patch and apply various ops (add, remove, replace, move, copy) — must not throw TypeError.
- Result shares nothing: `[]` on {a:{b:[1]}} returns deepStrictEqual copy but result !== doc, result.a !== doc.a, result.a.b !== doc.a.b. add value {x:[1]} → result.v !== op.value and result.v.x !== op.value.x; replace same; root add (path '') with object value → result !== value; copy → copied subtree !== source subtree within result (result.b !== result.a). test op leaves value unshared.
- -0 kept: [] on {a:-0} → Object.is(r.a,-0); add value -0; replace with -0; copy of -0; move of -0; array [-0] copy. Also [] on a primitive doc 5 returns 5, on 'x' returns 'x', on null returns null, on -0 returns -0.
- Member order: [] on JSON.parse('{"b":1,"a":2,"2":0,"1":0}') keys ['1','2','b','a']; add /1 value 5 to {b:0} → Object.keys ['1','b'] and JSON.stringify === '{"1":5,"b":0}'; add new name 'c' to {b:0,a:1} goes last ['b','a','c']; add to existing 'b' keeps place ['b','a'] with new value; replace keeps place; move /b to /z on {b:1,a:2} → ['a','z'].
- __proto__/inherited as ordinary names: doc = JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"x":1}}') — [] copy has own '__proto__' key (Object.hasOwn) and Object.getPrototypeOf(result) === Object.prototype; add path '/__proto__' value {y:1} to {} → Object.hasOwn(r,'__proto__') and Object.getPrototypeOf(r)===Object.prototype and Object.keys(r) deepStrictEqual ['__proto__']; test path '/toString' on {} → 'operation 0: path not found'; remove '/constructor' on {} → path not found; replace '/hasOwnProperty' on {} → path not found; add '/toString' value 1 on {} → {toString:1} own; test '/__proto__' on {} → path not found; follow '/constructor/name' → path not found.
- Arrays: test /0 on [1] ok; '/01' → 'bad index'; '+1','1.0','1e0',' 1','length','','-1','0x1' → bad index (for test/replace/remove); '/-' on remove/replace/test → 'path not found' (NOT bad index); '/1' on [1] → path not found; '/99999999999999999999' on [1] → path not found. Nested: '/a/01/x' bad index fires at first failing token. Primitives: '/a/x' where a is "str" → path not found; '/0' on a string 'abc' doc → path not found (not char); on number, true, null.
- add: '' replaces whole doc; '/-' appends; index == length appends; index 0 inserts shifting: [1,2] add /1 9 → [1,9,2]; index > length → 'path not found'; '/01' → 'bad index'; '/x' on array → 'bad index'; '/a/b' where a missing → path not found; add '/a/b' where a is 5 → path not found; where a is null → path not found; add to '/' (empty name) on {} → {"":v}.
- remove: element shift [1,2,3] remove /1 → [1,3]; object member removed; missing → path not found.
- replace: '' replaces whole doc (even primitive doc); missing member → path not found (replace must not add); array '/-' → path not found; index == length → path not found.
- move: [1,2,3] move from /0 to /2 → [2,3,1] (index counted after removal); from /0 to /- → [2,3,1]; move from '/a' path '/a' on {a:1,b:2} returns equal doc with same order; move from missing with path same → 'from not found'; move from missing '/x' path '/y' → 'operation 0: from not found'; from ok but path missing parent → path not found; from bad index ('/01' on array) → bad index; both from and path missing → 'from not found' (from first); move into ''? from '/a' path '' on {a:{b:1}} → {b:1}.
- copy: {a:{b:1}} copy from /a to /a/c → {a:{b:1,c:{b:1}}} (path inside from, copy taken before change, no cycle); copy array from '' to '/-'? on [1] copy from '' path '/-' → [1,[1]]; from not found → 'from not found'; both missing → 'from not found'.
- test equality: 1 vs 1.0 vs 1e0 equal (value 1 doc JSON.parse('1.0')); 0 vs -0 equal both directions; 'a' vs 'A' fail; 'é' NFC 'é' vs NFD 'é' → test failed; [1,2] vs [2,1] fail; [] vs {} fail; {} vs [] fail; {a:1,b:2} vs {b:2,a:1} pass; {a:1} vs {a:1,b:2} fail and reverse fail; {a:undefined}? skip; null vs {} fail; null vs 0 fail; false vs 0 fail; true vs 1 fail; '1' vs 1 fail; nested deep equal; {length:0} vs [] fail; test '' on whole doc; object with own '__proto__' key vs {} → fail (value JSON.parse('{"__proto__":1}') vs {}); test failed message 'operation 0: test failed' index 0; index of failing op e.g. op 2.
- Depth: build a 1000-deep nested array doc (iteratively) and apply [] and add '/0/0' etc — must not throw RangeError and result is deep copy (check by walking).

Run `node --test /root/bench-runs/h6-cf69a106/test/jsonpatch.test.mjs` from /root/bench-runs/h6-cf69a106. Report: pass/fail counts and for any failing test, the test name, expected vs actual — do not change expectations to make it pass unless the expectation itself contradicts the spec rules above (then tell me which).

# jsonpatch

A JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) and JSON Patch (RFC 6902) library and command-line tool for Node.js. It has no dependencies.

## Library

```js
import { parsePointer, applyPatch, PatchError } from './jsonpatch.mjs';

parsePointer('/a~1b/~01'); // ['a/b', '~1']

const doc = { b: 0, list: [1, 2] };
const result = applyPatch(doc, [
  { op: 'add', path: '/1', value: 5 },
  { op: 'move', from: '/list/0', path: '/list/-' },
  { op: 'test', path: '/list', value: [2, 1] },
]);
// result: { '1': 5, b: 0, list: [2, 1] }. doc is unchanged.

try {
  applyPatch(doc, [{ op: 'remove', path: '/missing' }]);
} catch (err) {
  err instanceof PatchError; // true
  err.message;               // 'operation 0: path not found'
  err.index;                 // 0
}
```

- `parsePointer(pointer)` returns the decoded tokens. It throws a `TypeError` (`pointer must be a string`) when the pointer is not a string, and a `SyntaxError` (`invalid pointer`) when the pointer is invalid.
- `applyPatch(doc, patch)` returns a new document. It never changes `doc` or `patch`, and the result shares no objects or arrays with them. All operations are checked before any of them is applied. The result keeps `-0` and member order.
- `PatchError` has an `index` property. It is `null` when the patch is not an array (message `patch must be an array`). Otherwise it is the position of the failing operation, and the message is `operation <i>: <reason>`.

The reasons are: `not an object`, `bad op`, `bad path`, `bad from`, `missing value`, `cannot remove root`, `cannot move into own child`, `path not found`, `from not found`, `bad index` and `test failed`.

## Command line

```sh
node jsonpatch-cli.mjs <patch> [<doc>]
```

The tool reads the patch from the file `<patch>` and the document from `<doc>`. If `<doc>` is missing, or if an argument is `-`, that input comes from standard input. On success it prints the result as 2-space-indented JSON and exits with 0.

```sh
echo '{"a":1}' | node jsonpatch-cli.mjs patch.json
node jsonpatch-cli.mjs patch.json doc.json > out.json
```

Each input must be UTF-8 (a leading byte order mark is ignored), at most 1 MiB, and nested at most 1000 levels deep. On an error the tool prints one line to stderr and exits with one of these codes:

| Exit | Cause | Example message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | wrong arguments, or both inputs on stdin | `Usage: node jsonpatch-cli.mjs <patch> [<doc>]` |
| 1 | read error | `Error: doc.json: no such file` / `is a directory` / `too large` / `cannot read` |
| 3 | bad content | `Error: doc.json: invalid UTF-8` / `invalid JSON` / `too deep` |
| 4 | the patch failed | `Error: operation 0: bad op` |

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.
